concepts.name: Linear Regression
concepts.description: A statistical modeling method that describes the linear relationship between a continuous predictor variable (X) and outcome variable (Y) to make predictions.

concepts.name: Intercept
concepts.description: The expected value of Y when X is 0, serving as the starting point of the regression line.

concepts.name: Slope
concepts.description: The expected change in outcome variable Y for each unit increase in predictor variable X.

concepts.name: Residuals / Error
concepts.description: The discrepancy between observed real data points and the values predicted by the regression line.

concepts.name: F-Test for Model Fit
concepts.description: A hypothesis test calculating the ratio of model-explained variance to error variance to assess overall model predictive utility.

concepts.name: Coefficient of Determination (R²)
concepts.description: An effect size metric representing the proportion of variance in outcome Y accounted for by the predictor model.

concepts.name: t-Test for Slope
concepts.description: A hypothesis test evaluating whether the slope coefficient differs significantly from zero.

concepts.name: Assumptions of Linear Regression
concepts.description: Required statistical criteria including interval/ratio scale data, linearity, homoscedasticity, no extreme outliers, and normally distributed residuals.

claims: Linear regression creates a predictive statistical model for Y based on X, unlike correlation which only tests for association without predictive directionality.
A linear model can be expressed mathematically as Y = Intercept + (Slope * X) plus residual error.
Goodness of fit is tested using an F-test comparing model variance (MS_model) to residual variance (MS_error).
R² quantifies the proportion of variance in the outcome variable Y explained by the predictor X.
A t-test for the slope coefficient evaluates the null hypothesis that there is no relationship between predictor X and outcome Y.
Assumptions for linear regression include continuous data, linear relationship, homoscedasticity, lack of extreme outliers, and normally distributed residuals.
summary: This document (Lecture 11 by M. Siromahov) introduces simple linear regression as a statistical modeling tool for predicting an outcome variable from a continuous predictor variable. It explains model components (intercept, slope, residual error), hypothesis testing (F-test for overall model fit and t-tests for slope significance), effect size via R², R implementation using lm() and summary(), standardized reporting guidelines, and core statistical assumptions.
